hunks.sol: “At first, I thought so too. But I was mistaken. I gave up the liquor I loved so much and secluded myself in the wilderness to calm my mind, yet nothing changed.”

hunks.baseline: “It means it isn’t because this old man’s mind has grown dull.”
hunks.sol: “It isn’t because this old man’s faculties have grown dull.”

hunks.baseline: Though the ceiling of the Buddha hall blocked his view, the profound gaze of the old monk seemed to pierce through it.
hunks.sol: Though the ceiling of the Buddha hall blocked his view, the old monk’s profound gaze seemed to pierce straight through it.

hunks.baseline: “The heavenly patterns are becoming distorted. Drawing closer, and moving faster.”
hunks.sol: “The heavenly patterns are falling into disarray. The disturbance is drawing closer, faster and faster.”

hunks.baseline: “A Morning Star appeared amid all of that. Even in those disordered heavens, I could see its light clearly.”
hunks.sol: “Then, amid all that, a Morning Star rose. Even in those chaotic heavens, its light was unmistakably clear.”

hunks.baseline: Hong Dao thought for a long moment, then shook his head.
hunks.sol: Hong Dao considered the question for a long moment, then shook his head.

hunks.baseline: “This is as much as I can say. Though the heavenly patterns are confused, they still retain their form, and the great trees rooted throughout the land will not be easily shaken. However…”
hunks.sol: “That is all I can say. Though the heavenly patterns are in turmoil, they still retain their form, and the great trees rooted throughout the realm will not be easily shaken. However…”

hunks.baseline: An unknowable light entered Hong Dao’s eyes.
hunks.sol: An inscrutable light entered Hong Dao’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: The words that followed held the wisdom of a sage, something only someone who was both the current Abbot of Shaolin—the sect hailed as the Murim’s greatest pillar for a thousand years—and deeply versed in the study of the heavens could display.
hunks.sol: The words that followed carried the wisdom of a sage—of the current Abbot of Shaolin, the sect hailed for a thousand years as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and of a man deeply versed in the study of the heavens.

hunks.baseline: “An unknowable calamity is approaching. Dark clouds gathering from somewhere will cover the sun and blanket the stars.”
hunks.sol: “An unknown calamity is approaching. Dark clouds will roll in from somewhere, covering the sun and swallowing the stars.”

hunks.baseline: A sky dyed in darkness, without a single ray of light.
hunks.sol: A sky steeped in darkness, without a single ray of light.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang imagined the scene and let one word escape like a groan.
hunks.sol: Imagining it, Jeok Cheongang let one word slip out like a groan.

hunks.baseline: “Dark Heaven. Yes, it will become just as you said…”
hunks.sol: “Dark Heaven. Yes, it will become just as you said—”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang hurriedly cut him off.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang hastily cut him off.

hunks.baseline: “No, that’s not what I meant. I just remembered something I heard from Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
hunks.sol: “No, that’s not what I meant. I remembered something Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, told me.”

hunks.baseline: “Jin Wikyung? I don’t know who that is, but are you saying he predicted this situation as well?”
hunks.sol: “Jin Wikyung? I don’t know the name, but are you saying he foresaw this situation as well?”

hunks.baseline: “More accurately, it appeared before them. I saw it with my own eyes.”
hunks.sol: “More accurately, they appeared before his family. I saw the evidence with my own eyes.”

hunks.baseline: He told him about the surviving remnants of the Head Elder’s faction, who were still alive despite the restrictions placed on them, and about everything that had happened up to that point. He also told him about the mysterious pill called the Temporary Strength Pill that he had taken from Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader.
hunks.sol: He told him about the surviving remnants of the Head Elder’s faction, who remained bound by the restrictions placed upon them, and everything they had learned so far. He also described the mysterious Temporary Strength Pill he had taken from Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung had passed all those facts to Jeok Cheongang, and Jeok Cheongang now passed them to Hong Dao.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung had told Jeok Cheongang everything he knew, and now Jeok Cheongang passed it all on to Hong Dao.

hunks.baseline: “It was astonishing. The restrictions placed on those men were so complex that even I could not easily break them, and the effects of that Temporary Strength Pill were bizarrely powerful.”
hunks.sol: “It was astonishing. The restrictions placed on them were so complex that even I couldn’t easily break them, and the effects of that Temporary Strength Pill were bizarrely powerful.”

hunks.baseline: “What a thing to happen.”
hunks.sol: “To think such a thing happened…”

hunks.baseline: “The hidden force that manipulated the Blade of Flowers from behind for decades. They are Dark Heaven.”
hunks.sol: “The hidden force that manipulated the Blade of Flowers from the shadows for decades. They are Dark Heaven.”

hunks.baseline: “Ha…”
hunks.sol: “Hah…”

hunks.baseline: After the story ended, Hong Dao let out a low groan and fell into deep thought.
hunks.sol: When the story ended, Hong Dao let out a low groan and sank into thought.

hunks.baseline: A long time passed before he finally opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: A long time passed before he finally spoke.

hunks.baseline: “It seems that the time has come for each of us to do what we must. I will prepare for the calamity with all my strength, and you…”
hunks.sol: “It seems the time has come for each of us to do what we must. I will devote all my strength to preparing for this calamity, and you…”

hunks.baseline: “You must stay beside the Morning Star. So it doesn’t fade easily.”
hunks.sol: “I must stay beside the Morning Star. Make sure its light isn’t easily extinguished.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang knew that protecting it was not the end of his task. He had to guard that light while making it shine even more brightly.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang knew his task did not end there. He had to protect that light while helping it shine even brighter.

hunks.baseline: “I won’t see you far off. We’ll save the rest of our reunion for another time.”
hunks.sol: “I won’t see you off. We’ll save the rest of our reunion for another time.”

hunks.baseline: Their farewell was long, but their meeting had been short.
hunks.sol: Their separation had been long, and their reunion short.

hunks.baseline: Remembering the words he had not managed to finish saying.
hunks.sol: As he left, he recalled the words he had never gotten the chance to say.

hunks.baseline: *It was a short meeting, but I enjoyed it.*
hunks.sol: *It was a short reunion, but I enjoyed it.*

hunks.baseline: Late that night, the young man and the old man left Mount Song and Shaoshi Peak.
hunks.sol: Late that night, the young man and the old man left Shaoshi Peak on Mount Song.

hunks.baseline: Their journey continued until the sun rose and set again.
hunks.sol: They continued walking until the sun rose and set once more.
